g.text: Judging a release by what is inside it
A funnel that gets more expensive at every step, and throws candidates out as early as it can.
Album not inside → out, whatever it is called
The rest set to skip before the download starts
a 20 GB discography costs one album
the same lie told about depth
Not the level — the drop. FFT with numpy
Not per track — one odd file does not decide a record
this tool's own tag are ever removed
Measured against files of known provenance: MP3 320 CBR drops 57 dB · MP3 V0 drops 12 dB ·
FLAC 16/44 drops 13 dB · FLAC 24/96 drops 3 dB.
A first attempt compared each track's highs to its loudest bin. That bin is always bass, so every
honest record read as cut at 17 kHz — including a 320 kbps file whose real shelf is 20.5.
Of ten torrents for one album, none declared its format. Lidarr classified all ten Unknown —
correctly: it cannot prove any is better. The one with 39 seeders was MP3.
Every number is printed, so the call can be overruled.
